title: Adaptive profile delta generator and runner affinity tagging
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our current benchmark harness publishes monolithic performance profiles which are expensive to produce, hard to diff between model versions, and often include runner-agnostic noise. Goal: Implement an incremental (delta) profile generator that emits compact, version-diffable artifacts and attaches runner-affinity tags so that downstream routing and pinning logic can make informed decisions. The feature should: 1) fingerprint datasets and prompt corpora to avoid re-running unchanged slices, 2) apply lightweight prompt mutation to expand coverage without full dataset duplication, 3) attach runner affinity metadata (e.g., kernel variants, quantization support, observed latency bucket) to each profile shard, and 4) produce a publishable artifact format that integrates with the Console rollout UI and Optimize recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Delta generator produces profile shards that are <= 25% size of full-profile for minor model changes
Dataset fingerprint prevents rerun when dataset+prompts checksum matches previous run
Runner affinity tags include: kernel_variant, quant_support, observed_p50_ms, observed_p95_ms, hardware_family
CLI: `harness profile publish --delta --base <artifact>` creates diff artifact and uploads to S3-compatible bucket
Console can render per-shard affinity tags in the model version profile page
Integration tests cover deterministic seeding and reproducible shard ordering
tasks: Design artifact schema for shard-level metadata (schema doc in drive)
Implement fingerprinting util for datasets and prompt corpora
Add prompt-mutation module (small paraphrase/templating) to generator
Wire runner adapters to emit observed stats and kernel tags
CLI flags for delta generation and base-artifact selection
Publish integration and Console display hooks
End-to-end test and perf validation on dedicated infra
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Storage vs fidelity — shard-level compression reduces storage but loses some contextual logs; we will keep raw logs for 7 days and compressed aggregates indefinitely. 2) Mutation aggressiveness — conservative mutation only for low-risk evaluation suites to avoid introducing synthetic distribution shift. 3) Runner tags may expose implementation details; tags will be normalized and namespaced to avoid user-facing confusion.

2025-03-03 - Aisha Raman: Design review completed. Agreed to namespace runner affinity tags with 'aff.' prefix (eg. aff.kernel_variant) to avoid collisions. Also approved retention policy for raw logs (7d) and aggregates (indefinite).
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint util and mutation module; integration test that runs generator against two model versions (v1 -> v1.1) and validates produced diff artifact size and deterministic ordering; end-to-end on staging with Console rendering; stress test with 50 concurrent shards to validate S3 and uploader reliability.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Mutation introduces evaluation noise -> Mitigation: conservative default mutation rate (10%) and ability to opt-out per-project
Risk: Tag proliferation -> Mitigation: registry of allowed affinity tags and normalization step during publish
Risk: Large number of tiny shards -> Mitigation: shard coalescing heuristic by size and runner similarity
